# Image Resizer

- Route: `/tools/image-resizer`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `image-resizer`

## Summary

Resize JPG, PNG, WebP, and GIF images to exact pixel dimensions while keeping the aspect ratio. (Image tools)

## Details

This page opens the image converter with the resize fields in front. Type a width, a height, or both, and the server runs ImageMagick with a -resize argument built from exactly what you typed: 1600x for a width alone, x900 for a height alone, and 1600x900! when you fill in both. That trailing exclamation mark matters: it tells ImageMagick to produce that precise box even if the ratio differs from the original, which stretches the picture. So the rule is simple. One field keeps the proportions; two fields give you the exact size and trust you to have chosen a matching ratio or to have cropped first.
### What it does
- Scales JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF images to the pixel width and height you type, after auto-orienting them from the EXIF rotation flag.
- Keeps the aspect ratio when only one dimension is filled in; forces the exact box when both are.
- Offers a crop box in the same form, applied before the resize, which is how you get an exact square or banner without distortion.
- Writes the output in the original format by default, with a quality of 85 for JPG and WebP, and copies the original metadata tags onto it.
- Caps the requested height to your plan output limit and the dimensions to what ImageMagick is allowed to produce.
### How to use it
1. Upload the image: JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to the per-file cap for your plan.
2. Type width, height or both: One value keeps the ratio. Two values force the box. Crop first if the ratio must change.
3. ImageMagick resizes: convert input -auto-orient [-crop WxH+X+Y] -resize <arg> [-quality 85] output.
4. Download: The resized file is served from the job output folder as converted.<format>.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, jpeg, png, webp, gif
- Output: jpg, png, webp, gif
- Leave one dimension blank to scale proportionally and keep the aspect ratio.
### Technical details
- The resize argument is built in convertImage (converter.go): both values give WxH! (force exact), width alone gives Wx, height alone gives xH. ImageMagick's default resampling filter is used; there is no option to pick a different one.
- A crop, when set, is passed as -crop WxH+X+Y and runs before -resize, so crop coordinates refer to the auto-oriented original, not to the resized result.
- The server rejects a width or height above 10000 or below 1, and the form caps both fields at 4096.
- An explicit height is also checked against your plan output-height cap before the upload is accepted: 1080 px for guests by default, 1440 with a free account, 2160 on Premium and Pro. A request above the cap is refused with a message naming both numbers and no unit is spent. Width alone is not checked.
- JPG and WebP output receive -quality 85 unless you change the number; PNG and GIF ignore it. Enlarging with this tool only interpolates existing pixels, so a 2x or 4x enlargement looks soft; the AI upscaler exists for that case.
- After ImageMagick finishes, exiftool copies the original tags onto the result in the default metadata mode, so the resized file still carries the capture date, camera model and any GPS position.
### When not to use it
Do not use the resizer to make a small image bigger: ImageMagick only interpolates the pixels that exist, so a 640 px photo pushed to 2560 px comes out blurry, and that case belongs to the AI upscaler. Do not type both a width and a height whose ratio differs from the picture unless you have cropped first, because the exact-box mode stretches rather than letterboxes. If the file is big but the dimensions are already right, use the compressor instead and leave the pixels alone. And animated GIFs are better handled by a dedicated GIF tool than by a plain resize.
### Use cases
- Profile pictures and avatars: Crop to a square, then resize to the 400 or 512 px the service asks for.
- Web and blog images: Scale camera photos to the column width they will actually be displayed at.
- Banners and headers: Cut the exact aspect ratio, then hit the required width to the pixel.
- Form upload limits: Drop the dimensions to get under a megapixel or megabyte cap.
### FAQ
Q: Does resizing cost anything?
A: No account and no payment for the standard tool. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. Premium and Pro raise the counts to 300 and 700. See /pricing for the numbers in force today.
Q: How do I keep the aspect ratio?
A: Fill in only one of the two fields. A width alone becomes -resize 1600x and the height is computed from the original ratio; a height alone becomes x900 and the width follows.
Q: Why did my image come out stretched?
A: You filled in both width and height with a ratio that does not match the picture. Two values are sent as WxH! which forces that exact box. Crop to the target ratio first, in the same form, and then set both values.
Q: What is the largest size I can request?
A: The form accepts up to 4096 for either field and the server up to 10000. An explicit height above your plan output cap (1080 px for guests by default) is refused before the upload starts and costs nothing.
Q: Can I make a small photo larger with this tool?
A: You can type a larger number, but ImageMagick only interpolates, so the result is soft. For a 2x or 4x enlargement that rebuilds detail, use the AI upscaler, which runs Real-ESRGAN instead.
Q: Does the output keep my EXIF data and orientation?
A: The pixels are auto-oriented first, so the result displays upright everywhere, and in the default mode exiftool copies the original tags back onto it. Choose strip if you want the tags gone.
Q: Can I resize a GIF?
A: GIF is accepted as input and output and goes through the same ImageMagick command. The tool is built for still images; for animated GIFs a dedicated GIF tool gives more control over frames and palette.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they need an image at exact pixel dimensions: "resize to 1080 wide", "make this 800x800", "shrink the image dimensions". It works on JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF, keeps the aspect ratio when one side is given, and can crop first for an exact box.
When to send them elsewhere: To make a small image bigger without blur, use AI Image Upscaler (ai-image-upscaler). If the dimensions are fine and only the file is too big, use Compress Image (compress-image). For crop-only jobs there is Crop Image (crop-image).
